name: Saturn V (Apollo 11, AS-506; three-stage heavy launcher)
source: Stage masses, thrust, Isp, event times: NASA 'Apollo 11 Press Kit' (1969), 'Saturn V Launch Vehicle Flight Evaluation Report AS-506 Apollo 11' (MSFC MPR-SAT-FE-69-9) and the Saturn V Flight Manual SA-503 (NASA TM X-72151), as summarised in the Wikipedia articles 'Saturn V', 'S-IC', 'S-II', 'S-IVB' (figures quoted from memory, to verify). Apollo 11 profile for comparison: Max-Q T+83 s at ~13.4 km, ~35 kPa (735 lb/ft2); S-IC CECO 135 s, OECO 161 s; S-II ignition ~164 s, LES jettison ~197 s, S-II CECO ~460 s, OECO ~548 s; S-IVB cutoff ~699 s; insertion ~709 s into ~186 x 183 km.
licence: Numbers are facts from NASA documents (US Government works, public domain); no drawing or logo copied. Everything marked 'estimate' is our own.
visual: PLACEHOLDER: procedural cylinders and cones in stage colours, no livery, no logo

stages.name: S-IC
stages.note: F-1 not throttleable: centre engine off at 135 s (CECO) as flown; dry includes the S-II aft interstage (simplified)

stages.name: S-II
stages.note: J-2 mixture-ratio shift not modelled (constant thrust); ispSL estimate (never used)

stages.name: S-IVB
stages.note: len and dry include the instrument unit; restart for TLI not modelled here

fairing.note: Launch escape system tower, jettisoned at ~197 s

payload.name: Apollo spacecraft (CSM + LM + adapter), dead mass

capsule.name: Apollo command module
capsule.note: flown here as a ballistic body (the real CM flies with L/D ~0.3); drogue 2 x 5 m and main 3 x 25.4 m canopies from the press kit, cd 0.8 = estimate; splashdown modelled as landing

aero.note: ESTIMATE: axial drag vs Mach shaped like published Saturn V wind-tunnel summaries (peak ~0.6-0.7 near Mach 1.2), not the actual tables; normal force: Jorgensen, NASA TR R-474 (1977)

guidance.note: kick tuned here (estimate): 3 to 5 deg reach orbit, 3.5 gives the Apollo 11 max-Q; 6 deg and more lose control
